component.name: log
component.title: Log Data
component.description: Log the exchanges that pass through a route, or their throughput, with an SLF4J logger.
component.label: core,monitoring

lazyStartProducer.label: producer
lazyStartProducer.description: Whether the producer should be started lazy (on the first message). By starting lazy you can use this to allow CamelContext and routes to startup in situations where a producer may otherwise fail during starting and cause the route to fail being started. By deferring this startup to be lazy then the startup failure can be handled during routing messages via Camel's routing error handlers. Beware that when the first message is processed then creating and starting the producer may take a little time and prolong the total processing time of the processing.

sourceLocationLoggerName.description: Whether the log endpoints use the source location of the endpoint in the route, the file or class name and the line number, as the logger name instead of loggerName. The sourceLocationLoggerName option of an endpoint replaces this option.

autowiredEnabled.label: advanced
autowiredEnabled.description: Whether autowiring is enabled. This is used for automatic autowiring options (the option must be marked as autowired) by looking up in the registry to find if there is a single instance of matching type, which then gets configured on the component. This can be used for automatic configuring JDBC data sources, JMS connection factories, AWS Clients, etc.

exchangeFormatter.label: advanced
exchangeFormatter.description: A custom org.apache.camel.spi.ExchangeFormatter for all log endpoints of this component. When set, the formatting options of the endpoints are not used. A bean named logFormatter in the registry takes precedence, and the exchangeFormatter option of an endpoint replaces both.

loggerName.description: The name of the SLF4J logger, also called the logging category. It is not used when an org.slf4j.Logger is given, by the logger URI parameter or as the only Logger bean in the registry, or when sourceLocationLoggerName resolves a name.

groupActiveOnly.description: Whether the groupInterval throughput logging skips an interval in which no new exchanges arrived. If false, it logs the statistics every interval.

groupDelay.description: The delay, in milliseconds, before the groupInterval throughput logging logs its first statistics. If not set, 1000 is used.

groupInterval.description: Turns on throughput logging: instead of each exchange, the endpoint logs statistics (the number of new and total exchanges and the messages per second) every interval, in milliseconds, from a background thread. It is not used when groupSize is set.

groupSize.description: Turns on throughput logging: instead of each exchange, the endpoint logs statistics (the number of exchanges and the messages per second) after every groupSize exchanges. It takes precedence over groupInterval, and the formatting options are not used.

level.description: The logging level of the log messages. OFF logs nothing.

logMask.description: Whether to mask sensitive values, such as passwords and passphrases, in the log message. If not set, the logMask setting of the route, or of the CamelContext, is used. A org.apache.camel.spi.MaskingFormatter bean named CamelCustomLogMask in the registry replaces the default masking.

marker.description: The name of an SLF4J marker to add to each log message.

plain.description: Whether to log only the body, without the Exchange[...] wrapper and the other parts. The stream, file and maxChars options still apply to the body.

sourceLocationLoggerName.description: Whether to use the source location of the log endpoint in the route, the file or class name and the line number, as the logger name instead of loggerName. If the source location is not known, for example because source location is not enabled, loggerName is used.

lazyStartProducer.label: producer,advanced
lazyStartProducer.description: Whether the producer should be started lazy (on the first message). By starting lazy you can use this to allow CamelContext and routes to startup in situations where a producer may otherwise fail during starting and cause the route to fail being started. By deferring this startup to be lazy then the startup failure can be handled during routing messages via Camel's routing error handlers. Beware that when the first message is processed then creating and starting the producer may take a little time and prolong the total processing time of the processing.

exchangeFormatter.label: advanced
exchangeFormatter.description: A custom org.apache.camel.spi.ExchangeFormatter that turns the exchange into the log message. When set, the formatting options of the endpoint are not used. If not set, the exchangeFormatter of the component, or a bean named logFormatter in the registry, is used.

maxChars.label: formatting
maxChars.description: The maximum number of characters to log. A longer body is cut at this length, and so is a longer log message, or each line of it with multiline. The global option CamelLogDebugBodyMaxChars, when set, replaces this limit for the body.

multiline.label: formatting
multiline.description: Whether to log each part of the exchange on its own line.

showAll.label: formatting
showAll.description: Show all parts of the exchange: the ID, the route group and route ID, the exchange pattern, all properties, the variables, the headers, the body type and body, the exception or caught exception, and its stack trace. It does not change multiline, maxChars, or the stream, file and Future options.

showAllProperties.label: formatting
showAllProperties.description: Show all of the exchange properties (both internal and custom).

showCachedStreams.label: formatting
showCachedStreams.description: Whether to log a body that is an org.apache.camel.StreamCache. The stream cache is reset after it is read, so the body can be read again later. If false, a placeholder is logged instead, unless showStreams is true.

showCaughtException.label: formatting
showCaughtException.description: Show the type and message of the exception of the exchange or, if it has none, of the caught exception (not the stack trace). Camel stores a caught exception in the CamelExceptionCaught exchange property, for example when doCatch catches it or onException handles it.

showException.label: formatting
showException.description: If the exchange has an exception, show the type and message of the exception (not the stack trace).

showExchangePattern.label: formatting
showExchangePattern.description: Show the exchange pattern (InOnly or InOut). When none of the formatting options is set, the endpoint uses the default output of the component, which shows the exchange pattern anyway.

showFiles.label: formatting
showFiles.description: Whether to log the content of a body that is a file, such as a java.io.File, a java.nio.file.Path or a file of the file or ftp components. If false, a placeholder with the file name is logged instead.

showFuture.label: formatting
showFuture.description: Whether to wait for a java.util.concurrent.Future body to complete and log its result. If false, the toString() of the Future is logged.

showProperties.label: formatting
showProperties.description: Show the exchange properties (only custom). Use showAllProperties to show both internal and custom properties.

showRouteGroup.label: formatting
showRouteGroup.description: Show the group of the route, if the route has one.

showStackTrace.label: formatting
showStackTrace.description: Show the stack trace of the exception that showException, showCaughtException or showAll shows. It has no effect without one of them.

showStreams.label: formatting
showStreams.description: Whether to log a body that is a stream, such as a java.io.InputStream or a java.io.Reader, or a stream cache. If false, a placeholder is logged instead. Beware that logging reads the stream, so later steps may not be able to read the body; use stream caching to avoid this.

showVariables.label: formatting
showVariables.description: Show the variables of the exchange, if it has any.

skipBodyLineSeparator.label: formatting
skipBodyLineSeparator.description: Whether to remove the line separators of the operating system from the body, so the body is logged on one line. If false, the body is logged as is.

style.label: formatting
style.description: The layout of the parts of the log message. Default separates them with a comma, as Label: value. Tab separates them with a tab, as Label: value. Fixed puts each value after a tab and the label padded to 20 characters.
